title: ChroPlate - IMAC
author: Alexandra Ehl
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8qqhvvw
materials: deionized water Cleaning solution 1: 6 M Guanidine chloride, 0.2 M Acetic acid Cleaning solution 2: 1 % Sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) Cleaning solution 3: > 95 % Ethanol Cleaning solution 4: 0.1 M Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) Cleaning solution 5: 0.2 M Acetic Acid Metal solution: 0.1 M Nickel(II) sulfate (or other metal ion of your choice) 20 % (v/v) Ethanol
Please choose below how you want to proceed.

steps.title: Prepare all buffers
steps.instruction:
Make the following solutions fresh on the day of use (buffers containing urea are unstable at room temperature):
- Binding buffer: 0.05 M sodium dihydrogen phosphate, 4 M urea, sodium chloride (adjust to pH 8.0 with NaOH). 
- Wash buffer: same composition as binding buffer (no imidazole). 
- Elution buffer: 0.05 M sodium dihydrogen phosphate, 4 M urea, 0.250 M sodium chloride, imidazole (adjust to pH 8.0 with NaOH). 
Aliquot and store at –20 °C for no longer than two months; do not freeze‑thaw more than once.

steps.title: Resuspend frozen bacterial pellet
steps.instruction: Weigh the frozen pellet, thaw on ice (or at room temperature if indicated), and resuspend in binding (or wash) buffer at 5 mL buffer per gram of pellet (alternative protocol: 3–5 mL g⁻¹). Add lysozyme and DNase I each at 0.01 % (mass/volume) corresponding to 0.1 mg mL⁻¹. Mix by pipetting. Optional: use ultrasonication according to instrument instructions. Pre‑chill a centrifuge to 4 °C.

steps.title: Lyse cells
steps.instruction: Incubate the resuspended cells with gentle end‑over‑end mixing, stirring or rocking for 30 min at 22 °C. If the target protein is protease‑sensitive, incubate for 60 min at 4–8 °C (or 15 min at 22 °C vs 30 min at 4–8 °C as alternative).

steps.title: Clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate for 30 min at >10 000 g, 4 °C. Carefully transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube. The equilibration of the ChroPlate can be performed while the centrifuge is running.

steps.title: Load metal onto ChroPlate (centrifuge)
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of nickel or cobalt solution (Cu²⁺ or Zn²⁺ may be used as alternatives) to each well. Place the ChroPlate on a deep‑well plate (use the dummy filter plate for counter‑balance) and centrifuge at 400 g for 60 s in a swing‑out rotor (alternative protocol uses 1000 g for 60 s).

steps.title: Load metal onto ChroPlate (vacuum)
steps.instruction: Assemble the vacuum device per the manufacturer’s instructions. Add 200 µL metal solution to each well, place the ChroPlate on a waste receptacle and apply 100 mbar vacuum for 2 min (metal options as above).

steps.title: Equilibrate with water (centrifuge)
steps.instruction: Empty the deep‑well plate, add 500 µL deionized water to each well, and centrifuge at 400 g for 2 min (alternative: 1000 g for 5 min). Repeat once.

steps.title: Equilibrate with water (vacuum)
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL deionized water to each well, place the ChroPlate on a waste receptacle and apply 100 mbar vacuum for 2 min. Repeat once.

steps.title: Equilibrate with wash buffer (centrifuge)
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL wash buffer to each well and centrifuge at 400 g for 2 min (alternative: 1000 g for 5 min). Repeat once.

steps.title: Equilibrate with wash buffer (vacuum)
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL wash buffer to each well, place the ChroPlate on a waste receptacle and apply 100 mbar vacuum for 2 min. Repeat once.

steps.title: Bind cleared lysate (centrifuge)
steps.instruction: Place the ChroPlate onto a clean deep‑well plate. Add up to 1.5 mL cleared lysate per well and centrifuge at 400 g for 2–10 min (viscous or >1 mL samples usually need >5 min). Keep flow‑through and wash fractions for later analysis. If the sample volume exceeds 1.5 mL, repeat the loading step.

steps.title: Bind cleared lysate (vacuum)
steps.instruction: Add up to 1.5 mL cleared lysate to each well and apply 100 mbar vacuum for 2 min. To collect flow‑through, install a deep‑well plate instead of the waste receptacle. Repeat loading if volume >1.5 mL. Adjust vacuum time or pressure for viscous samples.

steps.title: Wash plate (centrifuge)
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL wash buffer to each well and centrifuge at 400 g for 2 min. Repeat once; for higher purity repeat a third time (yield will decrease).

steps.title: Wash plate (vacuum)
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL wash buffer to each well, apply 100 mbar vacuum for 2 min. Repeat once; optional third wash for increased purity (yield will decrease). If wash fractions are needed, mount a deep‑well plate beneath the ChroPlate.

steps.title: Elute protein (centrifuge)
steps.instruction: Place the ChroPlate on a clean deep‑well plate. Add 300 µL elution buffer to each well and centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min (alternative protocols use 200 µL or 100 µL with 2 min centrifugation). Repeat the elution two more times into the same deep‑well plate. Note: additional elution steps increase recovery but lower final protein concentration.

steps.title: Elute protein (vacuum)
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL (or 100 µL) elution buffer to each well, place the ChroPlate on a clean deep‑well plate and apply 100 mBar vacuum for 2 min. Repeat two more times. As above, more elution cycles improve recovery but dilute the sample.

steps.title: Optional column cleaning (re‑use)
steps.instruction: For each column, sequentially add 500 µL of Cleaning Solution 1, invert 4–5×, centrifuge at 10 000 g for 1 min, discard flow‑through. Follow with two 500 µL washes of deionized water (invert, centrifuge, discard) before adding Cleaning Solution 2 and repeating the same steps. After the second cleaning solution, perform three final washes with deionized water. Add 500 µL metal solution, incubate 5 min with end‑over‑end mixing, centrifuge 10 000 g for 1 min, discard flow‑through, then wash twice more with water.

steps.title: Store columns
steps.instruction: Close the bottom of the column, add 500 µL 20 % ethanol, reseal the lid and store at 4–8 °C. For long‑term storage, dry the open column (top and bottom) in an oven at 60 °C for 2 h or overnight, ensure the bottom stopper is dry, attach the outlet, close the lid and keep at room temperature.
